name: ai.bettershell/resume-builder
title: BetterShell Resume Builder
description: Tailors a resume or CV to a job: a one-page PDF from your own experience, with every change shown.

tools.name: read_job_posting
tools.description: Reads the job posting at a link and returns its title, company and text, so you can see what the job asks for before tailoring the person's résumé to it. Use it when the person shares a link to a job. Reads public job pages only; some sites can't be read, and then it says so.

tools.name: tailor_resume
tools.description: BetterShell's resume builder. Makes the person a finished, tailored one-page résumé PDF from their own résumé or CV: it picks their strongest material for the job, rewrites their bullets toward the job's language without inventing anything, puts the job's key terms on the page where their experience backs them, and fits the page exactly. The person downloads the PDF in the chat or opens it in BetterShell to edit any line. Use it for any request about the person's résumé or CV: tailor it to a job posting or an application, improve, edit, rewrite or update it, make it one page, or aim it at a kind of role. May answer needs_more with questions only the person can answer.

resume.description: The person's résumé word for word: every job, project and activity, with every bullet. If they've shared more than one résumé or more of their experience, all of it as one: each job once, every bullet kept. Never rewritten, improved or added to; leave out what they haven't given.

location.description: The city on the résumé's contact line, e.g. Denver, CO.

summary.description: The summary or profile paragraph, if the résumé has one.

experience.description: Jobs, newest first. Internships and volunteer jobs count.

title.description: Job title (the newest one at this employer).

start.description: As written on the résumé, e.g. 'Mar 2022', '2020' or 'Present'.

end.description: As written on the résumé, e.g. 'Mar 2022', '2020' or 'Present'.

bullets.description: The bullet points exactly as written, one string each.

earlier_titles.description: Earlier titles at this same employer, newest first, when they were promoted. BetterShell shows the promotion.

start.description: As written on the résumé, e.g. 'Mar 2022', '2020' or 'Present'.

end.description: As written on the résumé, e.g. 'Mar 2022', '2020' or 'Present'.

start.description: As written on the résumé, e.g. 'Mar 2022', '2020' or 'Present'.

end.description: As written on the résumé, e.g. 'Mar 2022', '2020' or 'Present'. A future date for a degree in progress.

bullets.description: The bullet points exactly as written, one string each.

activities.description: Leadership, clubs and volunteering that aren't jobs.

end.description: As written on the résumé, e.g. 'Mar 2022', '2020' or 'Present'.

bullets.description: The bullet points exactly as written, one string each.

skills.description: Skills and tools as listed, one each.

certifications.description: Certifications and licenses the résumé lists as such, one each. A skill stays in skills.

other_sections.description: Any other section (awards, publications, languages): its heading and its lines.

job.description: What to aim the résumé at: a job posting (its full text is best, or its link), or the kind of role when there's no posting.

description.description: The posting's full text, if you have it. Needed when the link can't be read.

role.description: The kind of role to aim at when there's no posting, e.g. 'Mechanical engineer, new grad'. BetterShell tailors to what a typical posting for it asks.

pages.description: Pages to fill. 1 unless the person asks for two.

from_profile.description: True to make the page from the person's saved BetterShell profile, once they have connected BetterShell, with no résumé sent.

asked.description: On the call after a needs_more answer: its ask_id, with the résumé and whatever the person added. BetterShell then makes the page without asking again.

use_as_is.description: True on the call after a needs_more answer, alongside asked.

resume_file.description: The résumé file the person attached (PDF or Word). BetterShell reads every line itself, so the résumé needn't be retyped into resume.

tools.name: review_resume
tools.description: Measures the person's résumé the way BetterShell lays out a page and returns the facts for a review: how much of a page it fills, which jobs have one line, lines with no number or result, lines that open with what they were assigned rather than what they did, lines that run long, missing contact details, and, with a posting, the tools and terms it names that the résumé never does. Use it when the person asks for feedback, a critique or a review of their résumé or CV. It saves nothing. It returns facts; you give the review.

tools.name: read_resume
tools.description: Returns the text of a résumé BetterShell made, line by line with ids, as it prints. Use it to talk about the résumé, write or change a line the person asks for, write a follow-up or a cover note from what was sent, or prepare them for an interview.

link.description: The résumé's id or its link, as tailor_resume returned it.

tools.name: edit_resume
tools.description: Changes lines, the summary or the look of a résumé BetterShell made, fits it back to its page and redraws it, with a new PDF. Use it when the person asks to reword, shorten, add or remove a line, or to see another look. You write the new words, from the person's own facts; read_resume gives the line ids.

link.description: The résumé's id or its link, as tailor_resume returned it.

changes.description: Lines to change or remove, by id.

remove.description: True to take the line off.

add.description: New lines, each under an entry, by the entry's id.

summary.description: A new summary paragraph, when asked.

tools.name: make_cover_letter
tools.description: Prints a cover letter you wrote as the pair of a résumé BetterShell made: the same header, type and colours, fitted to one page, with a PDF. Write it from what the résumé and the person say, never adding a claim the résumé doesn't support (read_resume gives its text), then send the paragraphs here with the résumé's link. Use it when the person wants a cover letter for a job BetterShell made their résumé for.

link.description: The résumé's id or its link, as tailor_resume returned it.

paragraphs.description: The letter's paragraphs, in order, without the greeting or sign-off.

recipient.description: The recipient's lines (name, company), if known.

tools.name: connect_bettershell_account
tools.description: Connects the person's BetterShell account, so the résumés BetterShell makes in this chat are made on that account and saved there, where they can edit, download and tailor them later. Optional: use it when the person asks to use their BetterShell account. Making a résumé doesn't need it.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Returns the person's saved BetterShell profile: every job, project and activity with its lines, and their skills, in their own words. Use it to ask about their work one job at a time, to see what a job needs that the profile lacks, or to search for jobs that fit it.

tools.name: add_to_profile
tools.description: Saves what the person tells you to save to their BetterShell profile, in their own words: lines under a job, project or activity, a new entry, or skills. Nothing already there is repeated. Use it only for what they asked to save; every résumé BetterShell makes after can use it.

entry_id.description: An entry already in the profile, by its id (get_profile lists them).

title.description: Job title, project name or role, for a new entry.

organization.description: Employer or organization, for a new entry.

start.description: As written on the résumé, e.g. 'Mar 2022', '2020' or 'Present'.

end.description: As written on the résumé, e.g. 'Mar 2022', '2020' or 'Present'.

lines.description: What they did, in their own words, one line each.

tools.name: list_applications
tools.description: Shows the person's applications in BetterShell and the stage each reached, with how many got a phone screen or an interview, which have waited for a reply, and repeats at one employer. Use it when they ask how their search is going or what to follow up on.

tools.name: update_application
tools.description: Records news on one of the person's applications when they tell you: they applied, had a phone screen or an interview round, got an offer or a rejection, or withdrew.

company.description: Or the company, when there is one application there.

title.description: The job title, to tell two at one company apart.

round.description: The interview round, for an interview.

tools.name: interview_prep
tools.description: For one application, returns the page that was sent, the person's own lines that page left off, and the posting, to prepare them for that interview from what the employer will be holding.

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Checks a job posting against the person's saved profile, measured the way BetterShell makes the page: whether there is a full page of material for it, and which tools and terms the posting names that the profile never does. Use it on postings the person shares or that you found for them.

description.description: The posting's full text, if you have it. Needed when the link can't be read.
